data.title: CI
data.tagline: CI is the practice of automatically building and testing changes as they enter shared code, so integration problems appear early.
data.learningOutcome: You can tell whether a submission receives automatic, visible checks and use them for a merge decision.
data.description: A PR can automatically run lint, unit tests, and build, then write pass or fail back to the PR. This exposes issues before or just after merging. Manually testing once before release is not continuous integration.

learning.assumes: You know several people’s changes eventually meet in shared code.
learning.outcome: You can tell whether a submission receives automatic, visible checks and use them for a merge decision.

distinctions.label: CD
distinctions.explanation: CI automatically builds and tests changes as they enter a shared mainline. CD continues moving validated versions toward a releasable or released state.

explanation.title: Find combination problems with each change
explanation.text: A change that seems fine alone can fail with mainline code, dependencies, or configuration. CI repeats build and tests on a push or PR, keeping failures close to their originating commit.

explanation.title: Make results actionable
explanation.text: Checks should attach to a commit or PR and clearly show success, failure, and logs. The team can then block an unpassed merge or continue a passing version to testing.

data.boundary: CI is not one particular GitHub Actions file and not automatic production release. Its core is continuously integrating and automatically verifying changes; CD then handles how passing versions remain releasable or reach production.

lessonPractice.title: A team says it has CI, but only manually combines all branches and tests on Fridays. Is that right?

options.label: Not complete CI; tests do not run automatically with each change
options.feedback: Correct. CI gains value by automatic verification as each change approaches the shared line, not at the end.

options.label: It is CI; one full test run before merging is enough
options.feedback: Whether it runs automatically and continuously around changes determines whether it serves continuous integration.

options.label: It is not CI because passing checks do not automatically deploy to production
options.feedback: Automatic release belongs to CD; CI itself focuses on build and verification.

data.agentPrompt: Make every PR automatically run lint, build, and critical tests, with results attached to that PR. Do not allow merge when any check fails; after passing, provide the commit, check names, and results.
